events.content: Now I understand the setup: this is a Next.js 16 app with `cacheComponents` (PPR) enabled, but `page.tsx` does one blocking top-level fetch before rendering anything. That means there's no static shell to prerender — the entire page falls back to `loading.tsx`'s full-page spinner instead of streaming granular sections. I'll split the data fetching per-section and wrap each in its own `Suspense` boundary so the shell (`<h1>` + skeletons) prerenders statically and each section streams independently.

events.content:
The build now confirms `/` is a **Partial Prerender (◐)** route — previously the blocking top-level fetch made the whole page fully dynamic with no static shell. Build succeeds cleanly. Summary of the optimization: - **`app/page.tsx`**: removed the single blocking `await getDashboardData()` at the top. `Page` is now sync and renders the static shell (`

Dashboard

`) immediately, with three independent `` boundaries around `CardStatsSection`, `RevenueChartSection`, and `LatestInvoicesSection`. - **`app/data.ts`**: split the single dashboard fetch into three independent fetches (`getCardData`, `getRevenueData`, `getLatestInvoicesData`), so each section's data dependency is isolated to its own async component. - **`app/skeletons.tsx`**: per-section fallback skeletons so each Suspense boundary has a meaningful placeholder instead of the full-page spinner. Result: Next can now prerender the shell (h1 + skeletons) statically at build time and stream each dynamic section in independently as its data resolves, instead of blocking the entire page behind one fetch and falling back to `loading.tsx`'s full-page spinner.
